question.text: The specific heat $C$ of a solid at low temperature shows temperature dependence according to the relation $C=D T^{3}$, where $D$ is a constant and $T$ is the temperature is kelvin. A piece of this solid of mass $m \mathrm{kg}$ is taken and its temperature is raised from $20 \mathrm{K}$ to $30 \mathrm{K}$. The amount of heat required in the process in energy units is

solution.text:
Amount of heat required, $Q=\int d Q$ $=\int_{T_{1}=20}^{T_{2}=30} \mathrm{mcdT}$
Given, $C=D T^{3}$
$\therefore \quad Q=\int_{20}^{30} m D T^{3} d T=m D \int_{20}^{30} T^{3} d T$
$$
=m D \frac{1}{4}\left[(30)^{2}-(20)^{2}\right]=\frac{65}{4} \times 10^{4} m D
$$
